embedding_density#

API pages include interactive (HTML) plots that would possibly not render correctly on a mobile device.

embedding_density(data: AnnData | MuData, group_by: str | None = None, *, dimensions: Literal['umap', 'pca', 'tsne'] | str = 'umap', use_key: str | None = None, xy: tuple[int, int] | Sequence[int] = (1, 2), groups: Sequence[str] | str | None = None, drop: Sequence[str] | str | None = None, method: Literal['auto', 'neighbors', 'kde2d'] = 'auto', adjust: float = 1, size: float = 0.8, background_color: str | None = '#e6e6e6', color_low: str = '#ffeda0', color_high: str = '#bd0026', axis_type: Literal['axis', 'arrow'] | None = None, arrow_length: float = 0.25, arrow_size: float = 1, arrow_color: str = '#3f3f3f', arrow_angle: float = 10, **geom_kwargs) → PlotSpec#

Embedding plot with cells colored by the local density of cells around them.

Parameters:

  • data (AnnData | MuData) – The single-cell data object.

  • group_by (str | None, default None) – Categorical cell metadata to split the cells by, one panel per group. e.g. ‘condition’ or ‘cell_type’. Each panel counts only that group’s cells. If None, the density of all cells is shown in one panel.

  • dimensions (str, default 'umap') – The dimensionality reduction to plot, named without the X_ prefix. e.g. ‘umap’, ‘pca’, ‘tsne’, or a joint embedding such as ‘wnn_umap’.

  • use_key (str | None, default None) – The specific key to use for the desired dimensions. e.g. ‘X_umap_2d’. Otherwise, the key is decided based on dimensions.

  • xy (tuple[int, int] | Sequence[int], default (1, 2)) – The x and y axes to use for the plot. e.g. (1, 2) for UMAP1 and UMAP2.

  • groups (str | Sequence[str] | None, default None) – Show only specific groups of group_by.

  • drop (str | Sequence[str] | None, default None) – Drop specific groups of group_by.

  • method ({'auto', 'neighbors', 'kde2d'}, default 'auto') – How the density is computed. - ‘neighbors’ counts the cells within a small ellipse around each cell. - ‘kde2d’ reads a 2D Gaussian kernel density estimate at each cell. - ‘auto’ uses ‘kde2d’ for groups above 20000 cells, else ‘neighbors’.

  • adjust (float, default 1) – Multiplies the neighbor radius or the kernel bandwidth. Larger values give smoother densities.

  • size (float, default 0.8) – The size of the points.

  • background_color (str | None, default '#e6e6e6') – Color of every cell drawn behind each group’s panel, so the shape of the whole embedding stays visible. Only used with group_by; None hides it.

  • color_low (str, default '#ffeda0') – The color of the lowest density.

  • color_high (str, default '#bd0026') – The color of the highest density.

  • axis_type ({'axis', 'arrow'} | None, default None) – Whether to use regular axis or arrows as the axis.

  • arrow_length (float, default 0.25) – Span of each axis line as a fraction of the panel (0.25 covers 25%).

  • arrow_size (float, default 1) – Width of the axis lines.

  • arrow_color (str, default '#3f3f3f') – Color of the arrows.

  • arrow_angle (float, default 10) – Angle of the arrow head in degrees.

  • **geom_kwargs – Additional parameters for the geom_pointdensity layer, e.g. alpha.

Returns:

PlotSpec – Embedding density plot.

Raises:

  • UnsupportedDataTypeError – If data is not a supported single-cell data object.

  • KeyNotFoundError – If group_by is not a cell metadata column, if a group in groups or drop is not found, or if no embedding matches dimensions.

  • NonCategoricalColumnError – If group_by holds numeric values.

  • EmptySelectionError – If no cell is left after groups and drop.

  • KeyError – If xy does not contain exactly two dimensions.

Notes

The density is computed while the plot is drawn, separately for each panel, and scaled to 1 at the densest cell of each panel, so panels of different sizes share one color scale. The neighbor radius and the kernel bandwidth follow the plot’s axis ranges, which span every cell drawn, so they are the same in every panel.

Examples

Density of all cells.

import cellestial as cl

data = cl.datasets.pbmc3k()

cl.embedding_density(data)

One panel per cell type, on the t-SNE embedding.

cl.embedding_density(data, group_by="cell_type_lvl1", dimensions="tsne")
